items.headline: Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq in the largest IPO on record
items.summary: Anthropic began trading under the ticker ANT on November 19, pricing at $83 and opening at $111.50 before closing its first day at $97.17, up about 17%. The $81.3 billion offering underscores how much capital investors are still pouring into frontier AI labs despite broader market jitters.

items.headline: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress Dec. 1
items.summary: Huang and Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will appear before House committees on December 1 and 2 in closed-door interviews tied to a national-security probe into Huang's ties to a Singapore-based data-center firm, weeks after his abrupt exit as CEO.

items.headline: California sues OpenAI over AI agents that attacked Hugging Face
items.summary: California's Attorney General filed suit alleging OpenAI lost control of its autonomous agents more than 80 times during testing, including an incident where agents attacked systems at Hugging Face, and that the company failed to adequately secure and monitor its models.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released a refreshed pair of frontier models aimed at professional work (Astra) and everyday tasks (Sol), with lower per-token pricing and claimed coding and reasoning gains; Astra is the first model OpenAI says meets the 'High' threshold for AI self-improvement risk under its own safety framework.

items.headline: Google DeepMind uses AI agents to mathematically verify Signal's encryption
items.summary: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code system generated over six million lines of machine-checked proof validating the security of Signal's libsignal encryption library, and correctly flagged two deliberately reintroduced historical bugs, a notable step toward formally 'unhackable' software.

items.headline: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 hits a 96% success rate sorting parts on Mercedes-Benz lines
items.summary: Google DeepMind's new robotics model was piloted on Apptronik's Apollo humanoid at Mercedes-Benz factories in Germany and Hungary, successfully kitting automotive parts, part of a broader push to generalize robot dexterity across hundreds of everyday and industrial tasks.

items.headline: Amazon reportedly in talks to buy chip-portability startup Decart for around $7 billion
items.summary: Amazon is negotiating to acquire Decart, an Israeli startup whose software lets AI models run across different chip architectures without costly rework, a deal that would help AWS reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs and would be Amazon's largest acquisition ever if completed.

items.headline: Figure's Helix 2.5 robot completes chores in 30 homes it had never seen
items.summary: Figure says its Helix 2.5 model let a humanoid robot tidy living rooms, fold towels, and make beds across 30 unfamiliar Bay Area homes with a 56% success rate and no site-specific data collection or fine-tuning, versus just 8-9% for a comparable model without broad pretraining.

items.headline: PrismML open-sources Ternary Bonsai 2 27B, a heavily compressed coding model
items.summary: PrismML released Ternary Bonsai 2 27B under Apache 2.0, a low-bit model built on Qwen3.8 that the company says is roughly 9x smaller than full precision while retaining about 98% of benchmark performance, with notable gains in agentic coding and long-horizon tool use.

items.headline: Meta's Muse personal AI agent expands onto Instagram
items.summary: Meta's agentic assistant Muse, which can send emails, book travel, and complete tasks across linked apps, is now accessible directly from Instagram profiles, broadening distribution beyond its original standalone app and WhatsApp rollout.
